label: Cell structure matters only as the visible expression of forces and energy
claim: The study of visible cell structure has little value except as part of a dynamical investigation, because the activities of a cell are due to energy and forces, not to particular material particles or structures as such.
quote: In short it would seem evident that, except in relation to a dynamical investigation, the mere study of cell structure has but little value of its own.
scope: cells generally, including germ-cells and ova

label: The nucleus is spherical because it is an immiscible fluid drop under uniform tension
claim: The nucleus is almost always spherical because its fluid substance does not mix with the surrounding protoplasm, so it is bounded by a film of uniform surface tension and immersed in a medium transmitting uniform fluid pressure; where the cytoplasm becomes more solid (as in muscle cells or mucus-laden epithelial cells) the pressure becomes unsymmetrical and the nucleus is deformed.
quote: So long as the fluid substance of the nucleus is qualitatively different from, and incapable of mixing with, the fluid or semi-fluid protoplasm which surrounds it, we shall expect it to be, as it almost always is, of spherical form.
scope: nuclei of cells generally; contrasted with muscle and epithelial cells with stiffened cytoplasm
candidate_data: Single-cell 3D imaging with segmented nuclear shapes (Allen Cell Explorer, Image Data Resource) combined with published cytoplasmic and nuclear mechanics measurements.

label: Morphological polarity of the cell is the outward sign of a dynamical polarity
claim: The visible polarity of a cell (symmetry of structure about an axis, such as nucleus–centrosome or free–attached surface) is the outward expression of a real polarised distribution of forces, whose lines of force are made visible where particles of matter become strung together under those forces.
quote: The _morphological_ “polarity” is accompanied by, and is but the outward expression (or part of it) of a true _dynamical_ polarity, or distribution of forces; and the “lines of force” are rendered visible by concatenation of particles of matter, such as come under the influence of the forces in action.
scope: cells with recognisable axes of symmetry, e.g. ova, columnar and ciliated epithelial cells
measurable_quantities: orientation of granule or fibril alignment
candidate_data: Imaging datasets of polarised epithelial cells (Image Data Resource) and published intracellular force or electric-field measurements.

label: The alveolar meshwork of nucleus and cytoplasm is a surface-tension froth
claim: The alveolar 'reticulum' seen in the nucleus and cytoplasm is a froth or foam produced by the interacting surface tensions of two intermixed fluids of similar density striving to separate, and is not inherent in the nature of protoplasm.
quote: This phenomenon is nothing else than what we call in ordinary language, a “froth” or a “foam.” It is a surface-tension phenomenon, due to the interacting surface-tensions of two intermixed fluids, not very different in density, as they strive to separate.
scope: nuclear and cytoplasmic alveolar meshworks of cells
candidate_data: Live-cell and electron-microscopy image collections (Image Data Resource, EMPIAR) and published measurements of cytoplasmic phase separation.

label: Fine internal networks and granules seen in fixed cells are largely artefacts
claim: Fixation preserves the general outward form of small organisms and cells, but the minute internal networks and granules described as the structure of protoplasm are to a large extent artefacts of coagulating fixatives, although larger structures such as nucleus, vacuoles, centrosomes and the spindle are really present in the living cell.
quote: While this assumption is reasonable and justified as regards the general outward form of small organisms or of individual cells, enough has been done of late years to shew that the case is totally different in the case of the minute internal networks, granules, etc., which represent the alleged _structure_ of protoplasm.
scope: histological preparations of cells fixed with chemical reagents
measurable_quantities: presence and morphology of intracellular networks in living versus fixed cells
variation of fixed structure with fixative used
candidate_data: Paired live-cell and fixed-cell imaging studies and cryo-electron tomography datasets (EMPIAR) comparing preserved structure.

section: Spindle and asters as lines of force
label: Mitotic figures require a polarised force like magnetism, not mechanical traction
claim: The spindle and asters of dividing cells are lines of force of a bipolar field made visible by more permeable particles, like iron filings between magnet poles, and they cannot be explained by mere mechanical traction on a protoplasmic web but require some polarised and polarising force analogous to magnetism or electricity.
quote: any explanation which is based, like Rhumbler’s, on mere mechanical traction, is obviously inadequate, and we shall find ourselves limited to the hypothesis of some polarised and polarising force, such as we deal with, for instance, in the phenomena of magnetism or electricity.
scope: caryokinetic (mitotic) division of animal and plant cells
measurable_quantities: forces on chromosomes and spindle poles
candidate_data: Published spindle mechanics and microtubule imaging studies (Image Data Resource mitotic screens such as MitoCheck) bear on the mechanism.

section: Nucleus and chromatin in the field
label: Chromatin behaves as a diamagnetic body and moves to the equatorial plane
claim: In the bipolar field between the centrosomes the nucleus as a whole behaves as a body more permeable than the cytoplasm and is drawn in between the poles, whereas its chromatin, once broken up, behaves like a diamagnetic body, is repelled to the weaker parts of the field, and so collects in a peripheral circle on the equatorial plane.
quote: the fact is that the chromatin substance now _behaves_ after the fashion of a “diamagnetic” body, and is repelled from the stronger to the weaker parts of the field.
scope: nuclei and chromosomes of dividing cells
measurable_quantities: chromosome position relative to spindle poles over time
chromosome distribution on the metaphase plate
candidate_data: Live-cell time-lapse mitosis imaging datasets (Image Data Resource, Cell Tracking Challenge) give chromosome trajectories.

label: Differences of electric potential play a great part in cell division
claim: Differences of electric potential between cell constituents, and between parts of the egg, play a great part in cell division; the potential difference between animal and vegetative poles of a fertilised egg fluctuates or reverses at successive segmentations, and the electrical difference of chromatin is greatest at mitosis.
quote: Among other investigations, all leading towards the same general conclusion, namely that differences of electric potential play a great part in the phenomenon of cell division
scope: dividing cells and fertilised eggs (e.g. Fundulus, toad, turtle)
measurable_quantities: timing of potential reversals relative to cleavage
electrophoretic mobility of nuclei and cytoplasm
candidate_data: Published bioelectric measurements in eggs and embryos (vibrating-probe and voltage-dye studies) deposited in supplementary data or Dryad.

label: Every cell division results from conflict between surface tension and opposing forces
claim: In all cells the mechanical process of division must be explained as the result of a conflict between surface tension and its opposing forces, the division plane being set in the equatorial plane of the polar field.
quote: in all cells whatsoever, the process of division must somehow be explained as the result of a conflict between surface-tension and its opposing forces.
measurable_quantities: cortical tension at equator and poles during cytokinesis
orientation of cleavage plane relative to spindle axis
candidate_data: Published micropipette aspiration and cortical tension measurements during cytokinesis, and mitosis imaging datasets in the Image Data Resource.

label: Entry of the first spermatozoon raises the surface tension of the egg
claim: Because later spermatozoa fail to enter the egg after the first, an immediate consequence of sperm entry is an increase in the surface tension of the egg.
quote: other spermatozoa, subsequent to the first, fail to effect an entry, we may safely conclude that an immediate consequence of the entry of the spermatozoon is an increase in the surface-tension of the egg
measurable_quantities: egg surface tension or cortical tension before and after sperm entry
candidate_data: Published measurements of egg cortical stiffness and polyspermy block in sea urchin, frog and mouse eggs.

label: The pronuclei travel curved paths and meet before reaching the centre of the egg
claim: Given an attraction between the male and female pronuclei and a force drawing them toward the egg centre, their paths lie within the triangle formed by the two bodies and the centre, are curved (convex toward the line joining them) unless they start on a diameter, and the pronuclei meet a little before the centre and then travel straight to it.
quote: (2) unless the two bodies happen to lie, to begin with, precisely on a diameter of the cell, their paths until they meet one another will be curved paths, the convexity of the curve being towards the straight line joining the two bodies; (3) the two bodies will meet a little before they reach the centre;
scope: pronuclear migration in fertilised eggs (e.g. frog)
measurable_quantities: 3D trajectories of male and female pronuclei
position of pronuclear meeting relative to egg centre
candidate_data: Live 3D time-lapse imaging of pronuclear migration in sea urchin, C. elegans or mouse zygotes (Image Data Resource and published supplementary data).

label: Mitotic phenomena follow from simple physical assumptions and have secondary significance
claim: Most if not all of the intracellular phenomena of mitosis follow inevitably from very simple assumptions about the physical constitution of the cell and a simple distribution of polarised forces within it, and are likely to prove of only remote and secondary biological significance.
quote: Most, if not all of them, would seem to follow immediately and inevitably from very simple assumptions as to the physical constitution of the cell, and from an extremely simple distribution of polarised forces within it.
scope: intracellular phenomena of cell division in plants and animals

label: Details of mitosis vary among close relatives and are not specific to the organism
claim: The details of mitosis (presence of visible caryokinesis, position of the field of force, number of chromosome groups, chromosome form and arrangement) vary greatly even among closely related organisms or within one species, and are not specifically related to the organism in which they occur.
quote: there seem to be strong grounds for believing that these and many similar phenomena are in no way specifically related to the particular organism in which they have been observed, and are not even specially and indisputably connected with the organism as such.
scope: mitosis in plants and animals, e.g. Copepods, Ascaris megalocephala
measurable_quantities: mitotic mode (open or closed, centrosomal or acentrosomal)
candidate_data: Comparative cytology compilations of mitotic types across eukaryotes combined with phylogenies from the Open Tree of Life.

label: Chromosome numbers of germ-nuclei mostly lie between six and sixteen
claim: Although chromosome number is constant within a species, the range of numbers across plants and animals is small: few organisms have fewer than six chromosomes in the germ-nuclei and fewer still have more than sixteen.
quote: (as regards the germ-nuclei) few organisms have less than six chromosomes, and fewer still have more than sixteen
scope: germ-nuclei (haploid chromosome number) of plants and animals
candidate_data: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB) for plants and published animal karyotype compilations.

label: Early embryological categories seldom coincide with phylogenetic classification
claim: Early embryological data, up to and well beyond segmentation, are a subject for physiological and physical investigation, and their categories (yolk content, chromosome form and number, radial, bilateral or spiral cleavage) will only seldom and accidentally coincide with the natural or phylogenetic classification of the systematist.
quote: But we have little right to expect, and in point of fact we shall very seldom and (as it were) only accidentally find, that these embryological categories coincide with the lines of “natural” or “phylogenetic” classification which have been arrived at by the systematic zoologist.
candidate_data: Comparative datasets of egg size and cleavage type mapped onto animal phylogenies (Open Tree of Life; published egg-size compilations on Dryad).

section: The cell as a sphere of action
label: Surface tension gives the cell its outline and morphological individuality
claim: The cell is a sphere of action of localised forces, of which surface tension gives the cell its outline and individuality; partial versus total segmentation of eggs, and unicellular versus multicellular organisation, differ in whether surface tensions succeed in forming visible separations between cells.
quote: surface-tension is the particular force which is especially responsible for giving to the cell its outline and its morphological individuality.
scope: cells, segmenting eggs, Infusoria and small Turbellaria
candidate_data: Published measurements of cortical and interfacial tension in embryos combined with embryo imaging datasets.

label: The centrosome is essentially a centre of force, not necessarily a material body
claim: The centrosome is essentially a dynamic centre of force, which may or may not consist of a visible concentration of matter but tends to produce one, as shown by cells that live without visible centrosomes and centrosomes that disappear and form anew.
quote: We may safely take it that the centrosome, or the “attraction sphere,” is essentially a “centre of force,” and that this dynamic centre may or may not be constituted by (but will be very apt to produce) a concrete and visible concentration of matter.
scope: centrosomes of animal and plant cells
candidate_data: Published studies of acentrosomal spindles and de novo centriole formation, and cell imaging datasets (Allen Cell Explorer).

label: A continuous field of force shapes the whole organism regardless of its cells
claim: The multicellular organism is not a colony of independent cells: a continuous field of force runs through the entire organism, not restricted to protoplasmic continuity, and shapes it independently of the number, size and form of its cells.
quote: And such a continuous field of force, somehow shaping the whole organism, independently of the number, magnitude and form of the individual cells, which enter, like a froth, into its fabric, seems to me certainly and obviously to exist.
measurable_quantities: organ shape versus cell number and cell size
effect of altered cell size or number on organ form
candidate_data: Published experiments on polyploid or cell-number-altered organisms (e.g. plant leaf and Drosophila wing size studies) with organ morphometrics.
